b1.texto:
These four phrases are useful in any Spanish class:

- **¿Cómo se dice «table»?** to find out a word
- **¿Cómo se escribe?** to find out the letters
- **¿Qué significa?** to find out the meaning
- **Más despacio, por favor.** to ask someone to repeat it

And if you haven't understood a thing: **No entiendo.**
b4.texto:
Spanish has two letters that English doesn't use:

- **la eñe (ñ)**: it sounds like «ny»
- **la jota (j)**: it sounds like a breathed h, rougher

And one letter that exists but never sounds: **la hache (h)**. That's why «hola» is pronounced «ola».
b4.titulo: Two new letters and one that stays silent
b5.f0.texto: Ana opens the notebook to the first page and writes her name in capital letters.
b5.f1.texto: The teacher approaches and asks her to spell it aloud for the whole class.
b5.f2.texto: Ana hesitates on the last letter and doesn't remember well whether it has an accent mark.
b5.f3.texto: “Ask,” the teacher says to her calmly.
b5.f4.texto: Nobody laughs because everyone is learning exactly the same thing.
b5.f5.texto: By the end of the morning, the notebook holds twenty new words, each with its letters spaced out clearly.
b5.f6.texto: Ana reads them very slowly, like someone trying out a musical instrument for the first time.
b5.f7.texto: Before putting the notebook in her bag, she writes the phrase “más despacio, por favor” in the margin.
b5.f8.texto: She knows she'll need it many more times.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «se dice» is used to ask for a word.
b6.o1.refuerzo: That asks about the letters, not about the word.
b6.o2.refuerzo: That asks for the meaning of a word you've already heard.
b6.pregunta: You want the Spanish word for «table». What do you ask?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Entiendo» goes with «yo», which is left out here.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Entiende» goes with él, ella or usted.
intro: In class you need four questions: how to say something, how to spell it, what it means and how to ask someone to repeat it.
p.España.consejo: It's written with eñe and has no vowel in front of it.
p.deletrear.consejo: To say a word letter by letter.
p.el abecedario.consejo: It's the list of the letters. You can also say «el alfabeto».
p.la eñe.consejo: The letter ñ. It sounds like «ny» in «canyon».
p.la hache.consejo: The letter h. In Spanish it never sounds.
p.la jota.consejo: The letter j. It sounds like a rougher English h.
p.la mesa.consejo: The s of «mesa» is always voiceless and strong.
p.no entiendo.consejo: The most useful phrase in any class.
p.por favor.consejo: The v is pronounced like a soft b.
p.qué significa.consejo: To ask for the meaning of a word.
p.repite.consejo: It's «repetir» with «tú»: you say it to the other person.
p.se dice.consejo: It's used to ask what something is called.
p.se escribe.consejo: To ask about the letters of a word.
p.mesa.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -a: «la mesa». The «e» is always clear, never like the English «ay».
p.eme.consejo: The letter «m» is called «eme» in Spanish. It starts with a vowel sound, so it is «E-me».
p.pronuncia.consejo: In Spain «c» before «e» or «i» sounds like the «th» in «think». So it is «pro-NUN-thya».
p.página.consejo: The accent mark shows the stress on the first syllable. Before «i», the «g» sounds like a soft «h».
p.letras.consejo: «letra» is feminine: «la letra». In the plural it adds -s and the article becomes «las».
p.mayúsculas.consejo: It comes from «mayor», bigger. Its stress falls on the «ú», so say «ma-YUS-cu-las».
p.acerca.consejo: It belongs to «acercarse», to come closer. The «c» before «e» sounds like «th», and «ca» like «k».
p.deletree.consejo: After «le pide que», Spanish uses the subjunctive, so «deletrear» becomes «deletree». Stress: de-le-TRE-e.
p.toda.consejo: It agrees with «clase», which is feminine. The masculine form is «todo», as in «todo el grupo».
p.duda.consejo: Same spelling as the noun «duda», doubt. Here it is the verb «dudar»: «ella duda». Stress on «DU».
p.última.consejo: The feminine of «último». Its stress falls on the first syllable, so it always wears an accent mark.
p.recuerda.consejo: Its root is «recordar», to remember. The «c» before «u» is hard, like «k»: «re-KWER-da».
p.calma.consejo: It is a feminine noun: «la calma». It appears in «con calma», meaning without rushing.
p.ríe.consejo: The accent mark splits the two vowels into two syllables: «RI-e». It is not one syllable like «rye».
p.aprendiendo.consejo: The «-iendo» ending is the gerund: an action happening now, like «learning». It comes from «aprender».
p.exactamente.consejo: Made from «exacto» plus «-mente», like the English «-ly». The «x» sounds like «ks».
p.guarda.consejo: Before «a», «gu» sounds like «gw»: «GWAR-da». Think of «guardia», a guard.
p.palabras.consejo: Its singular «palabra» is feminine: «la palabra», «las palabras». The stress falls on «LA».
p.nuevas.consejo: It agrees with «palabras», which is feminine plural. Remember that Spanish «v» sounds like «b».
p.separadas.consejo: From «separar», to split apart. The «-adas» ending matches «letras», which is feminine and plural.
p.lee.consejo: Two clear sounds, «le-e», from «leer». The object pronoun «las» goes before the verb: «las lee».
p.instrumento.consejo: Stress falls on «MEN», so say ins-tru-MEN-to. Many words ending in «-mento» work the same way.
p.musical.consejo: Comes from «música». The ending «-al» is common in Spanish adjectives, like «normal» and «personal».
p.libreta.consejo: Stress is on «BRE»: li-BRE-ta. The last «a» is short and open, as in «casa».
p.anota.consejo: Related to the word «nota». The stress falls on «NO»: a-NO-ta.
p.frase.consejo: Stress is on «FRA». It looks like the English «phrase», but the «s» is pronounced clearly.
p.corta.consejo: It agrees with «frase», a feminine word, so it ends in «-a». Stress is on «KOR».
p.margen.consejo: Before «e», the «g» sounds like a soft «h»: MAR-hen. It is masculine: «el margen».
p.entiendo.consejo: The stem changes «e» to «ie», as in «pensar» which gives «pienso». Stress falls on «TYEN».
p.entiendes.consejo: Same stem change as «entiendo», now for «tú»: «entiendes». The stress still falls on «TYEN».
p.entiende.consejo: The stem change appears again, now for «él» or «ella»: «entiende». Stress stays on «TYEN».
